risk_assessment.rationale: The use of an obfuscated (encoded) PowerShell payload is a common malware technique, but the decoded command simply verifies the presence of a node_modules folder – a routine operation for many legitimate applications.  No evidence of persistence mechanisms, lateral movement, data exfiltration, or other malicious activity was observed in this event.  Consequently the alert is classified as medium‑severity with medium confidence: it warrants analyst review but does not trigger an immediate high‑priority response.

recommended_actions_freeform_experimenta: Expand the scope of monitoring to capture any other instances where Cursor.exe or related processes invoke PowerShell with an encoded command, even if the decoded payload appears benign; a single trivial check can be a foothold for more complex scripts that are obfuscated in subsequent stages.

Perform a forensic integrity check on the Cursor.exe binary itself—compare its hash against known good releases and scan it for embedded malicious code or hidden modules that could be activated by the `--ms-enable-electron-run-as-node` flag.

Inspect the contents of the node_modules directory referenced by the decoded command; look for recently added or modified packages, especially those with suspicious names or unusually large sizes, which might indicate a compromised dependency injection.

Correlate this event with other system telemetry such as scheduled tasks, registry Run keys, or service creation that may have been triggered by Cursor.exe around the same timestamp to uncover potential persistence mechanisms.

If possible, isolate the user account (derek.tan) and conduct a host-based behavioral analysis—monitor outbound network connections, file system changes, and process tree expansions—to determine whether this encoded PowerShell invocation is part of a broader malicious workflow.

Leverage threat intelligence feeds to see if the domain dev-dtan06.victimcorp.com or any other related domains have been observed in known campaigns; even an unknown domain can be a sign of a custom command‑and‑control infrastructure.
Document and retain all logs surrounding this event for future reference, as encoded PowerShell usage is a common evasion technique that may surface again under different guise.
triage_rationale_experimental: The encoded PowerShell command performs only a trivial file‑system check, yet it is executed by an application (Cursor.exe) with a suspicious launch flag and from a user account that has not been previously validated; without additional malicious indicators the event cannot be confidently classified as benign or malicious.
